title: DGR: Differentiable Global Router
problem: Modern VLSI design flows require fast and high-quality global routers capable of handling hundreds of thousands of nets while minimizing routing overflow. Existing routers struggle to simultaneously optimize wirelength and via count in congested circuit layouts.
motivation: Efficient global routing is essential for optimizing circuit performance, power consumption, and silicon area in modern VLSI design.
method: DGR converts the circuit routing problem by representing all possible routes as a directed acyclic graph forest (a data structure encoding wiring patterns) and reformulating it as continuous optimization instead of discrete yes/no choices. It then uses GPU-accelerated deep learning methods—specifically gradient-based optimization techniques—to efficiently find good routing solutions. It simultaneously selects routing paths for all hundreds of thousands of circuit connections by choosing between 2-pin direct connections and Steiner trees (branching routes connecting multiple points), considering all interdependencies globally.
key_novelty: DGR solves circuit routing by reformulating it as a differentiable continuous optimization (solvable via calculus on GPUs) rather than discrete yes/no choices, enabling simultaneous optimization of hundreds of thousands of connections.
contributions: DGR: a fully differentiable global router supporting concurrent optimization of massive numbers of nets
Routing DAG forest representation enabling coordinated global routing path selection
Continuous relaxation of discrete routing problem solved via GPU-accelerated differentiable computing
Demonstrated 0.95-4.08% wirelength reduction and 1.28-2.54% via count reduction with improved scalability

metrics.other: wirelength reduction 0.95-4.08%, via reduction 1.28-2.54%, favorable runtime and memory scalability
